question: Tell me about a time you witnessed unethical or questionable behavior at work. What did you do?

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you witnessed unethical or questionable behavior at work. What did you do?

I noticed a teammate reusing internal test data that contained customer PII in a demo for another team. I first checked our data policy, then told them directly it looked off. They brushed it off, so I looped in my manager with the policy link and the exact files.
What was the outcome and how did your teammate react later?
Manager had the data scrubbed and we switched to synthetic data. Teammate was annoyed at first but later asked me to review another script.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you witnessed unethical or questionable behavior at work. What did you do?
Junior IC noticed teammate using customer PII in demo data
Checked policy first, spoke directly, then escalated to manager with specifics
Outcome: data replaced with synthetic set; teammate later asked for review help
Quote: 'I looped in my manager with the policy link and the exact files'
Follow-up: Asked about teammate reaction; candidate described short-term friction then improved collaboration
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Integrity, Ethics & Trust on the junior question. The candidate described spotting customer PII reused in a demo, verifying the policy, addressing the teammate directly, and escalating with concrete details when needed. The outcome was limited to their immediate work but showed ownership without overstepping. This meets expectations for 0-2 years: they owned their observation and used the right channel rather than ignoring or gossiping. Biggest strength is the direct-then-escalate sequence with a clear quote on how they documented the handoff.

I saw someone copy a slide deck from another team and change the date. It felt off but I didn't want to get involved so I just made sure my own slides were original.
Did you mention it to anyone or check the policy?
No, I figured it was their problem. I stayed out of it.

junior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for Integrity, Ethics & Trust on the junior question. The candidate observed a copied deck with an altered date but explicitly decided to stay out of it without checking policy or informing anyone. This shows no ownership even at the individual level expected of juniors. The story stays local and passive. Biggest gap is the absence of any attempt to address or escalate, which signals weak calibration on when to act.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you witnessed unethical or questionable behavior at work. What did you do?

A partner team was overstating feature readiness in a joint customer presentation to close a deal. I pulled the partner lead aside with the actual status, then suggested we both send a corrected note to the account team before the call.
How did you handle pushback and what was the cross-team result?

They pushed to keep the slide; I documented the discrepancy in email to both managers and offered a revised version. Deal moved forward with accurate timeline and we avoided a later escalation from the customer.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you witnessed unethical or questionable behavior at work. What did you do?
Senior saw partner team overstating readiness in joint deck
Addressed partner lead directly then sent joint correction to account team
Outcome: accurate timeline used; avoided customer escalation
Quote: 'I documented the discrepancy in email to both managers and offered a revised version'
Follow-up: Asked about pushback; candidate described documenting and offering fix
senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Integrity, Ethics & Trust on the senior question. The candidate identified overstated readiness in a shared customer deck, addressed the partner lead first, then used email to both managers with a proposed fix. The result protected the customer relationship across teams without authority. This aligns with 3-7 year expectations: influence without authority and cross-team impact. Biggest strength is the documented escalation path that kept the deal intact while correcting the record.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you witnessed unethical or questionable behavior at work. What did you do?

Two of my directs were splitting a contractor's hours across two projects to hide budget overrun. I had separate 1:1s, explained the policy violation, and required corrected time sheets plus a joint plan to surface the overrun to finance.
How did you handle performance and team outcome?
Both engineers received a written expectation note. We adjusted the project plan openly and the team hit the next quarter without further issues. One engineer later thanked me for the clarity.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you witnessed unethical or questionable behavior at work. What did you do?

Quote: 'I had separate 1:1s, explained the policy violation, and required corrected time sheets'

manager.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Integrity, Ethics & Trust on the manager question. The candidate identified two directs splitting contractor hours to hide an overrun, addressed each in 1:1s, enforced corrected reporting, and required an open plan to finance. The team outcome improved with no recurrence. This matches manager expectations: handling underperformance, creating team leverage through clear standards, and owning the result. Biggest strength is the combination of individual accountability and systemic fix.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you witnessed unethical or questionable behavior at work. What did you do?

During diligence for an acquisition we discovered the target had been selectively reporting churn metrics to investors. I paused the deal, brought the finding to the board audit committee, and required full data re-audit before any further talks.
What was the long-term org impact and trade-off?
Deal was terminated. We updated our own diligence checklist and later applied the same standard to two other targets, avoiding similar risk. Board noted the decision as precedent for future M&A.

Quote: 'I paused the deal, brought the finding to the board audit committee'

exec.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Integrity, Ethics & Trust on the exec question. The decision set an org-level precedent and changed future diligence. This fits 10+ year expectations: strategic judgment under ambiguity and long-term org leverage over short-term deal pressure. Biggest strength is the willingness to kill the deal and institutionalize the learning.
